question.text: Under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act, 2002 (PMLA) and its Maintenance-of-Records Rules, an AIF as a reporting entity must maintain records of which of the following cash-transaction thresholds?

answer.text: Cash transactions > INR 2 lakh, reported weekly to FIU-IND
Cash transactions > INR 10 lakh (single) OR a series of integrally-connected cash transactions individually below INR 10 lakh, but monthly aggregate exceeds INR 10 lakh
No cash threshold; only STRs are reported

explanation.text: The Logic: PMLA reporting entities (including AIFs) must maintain records of all cash transactions exceeding INR 10 lakh (single transaction), as well as a series of integrally-connected cash transactions individually below INR 10 lakh where the monthly aggregate exceeds INR 10 lakh. Suspicious transactions (STRs) must be reported regardless of amount. The Trap: Option A fabricates an INR 2 lakh weekly threshold. Option C uses INR 50 lakh (too high). Option D ignores the cash-record obligation entirely. Note: Workbook page 382 contains the PMLA transaction-record thresholds (single transaction and integrally-connected series), and page 383 supports the suspicious-transaction reporting context.
